scenes.visual: Title card: Mark It, Move It.

scenes.tts: How do you follow a cell that leaves home?
scenes.visual: A gold cell leaves the neural tube and vanishes among grey cells.
scenes.narration: How do you follow a cell that leaves home?

scenes.tts: You have to mark it before it goes. And the mark has to last.
scenes.visual: The gold cell reappears with a small tag on it.
scenes.narration: You have to mark it before it goes. And the mark has to last.

scenes.tts: Julia Platt opened the question in eighteen ninety three, working on the mudpuppy, a salamander.
scenes.caption: Julia Platt opened the question in 1893, working on the mudpuppy, a salamander.
scenes.visual: A mudpuppy sketch, the year 1893 on screen.
scenes.narration: Julia Platt opened the question in 1893, working on the mudpuppy, a salamander.

scenes.tts: In fixed sections, she followed cells from the crest into the arches, where head cartilage forms.
scenes.visual: A series of fixed sections in order; the pale cells move into the branchial arches.
scenes.narration: In fixed sections, she followed cells from the crest into the arches, where head cartilage forms.

scenes.tts: Cartilage was supposed to be mesoderm, and her evidence was indirect. The claim was long doubted.
scenes.visual: A rule card, cartilage comes from mesoderm, with a crack across it. Note: fixed sections, no living cell labelled.
scenes.narration: Cartilage was supposed to be mesoderm, and her evidence was indirect. The claim was long doubted.

scenes.tts: The lasting mark came from Nicole Le Douarin. Quail nuclei carry a dense block of chromatin. Chick nuclei lack it.
scenes.visual: Two stained nuclei side by side: quail with a dark block by the nucleolus, chick without.
scenes.narration: The lasting mark came from Nicole Le Douarin. Quail nuclei carry a dense block of chromatin. Chick nuclei lack it.

scenes.tts: The mark is built into the cell. It neither fades nor dilutes as cells divide.
scenes.visual: A quail cell divides several times; every daughter keeps the dark block.
scenes.narration: The mark is built into the cell. It neither fades nor dilutes as cells divide.

scenes.tts: Graft quail neural tube into a chick at the same level. Then map where the quail cells go.
scenes.visual: A short segment of quail tube replaces chick tube at the same level; later section shows marked cells in a ganglion.
scenes.narration: Graft quail neural tube into a chick at the same level. Then map where the quail cells go.

scenes.tts: But a same-level graft cannot say why. Origin and route are tangled together. To separate them, move the cells.
scenes.visual: The two arrows, origin and route, twist together; then a hand lifts a graft to a new level.
scenes.narration: But a same-level graft cannot say why. Origin and route are tangled together. To separate them, move the cells.

scenes.tts: Predict. Take trunk crest from the adrenal level. At home it makes cells that release noradrenaline and adrenaline. Move it into the neck. Where will it go, and what transmitter will it use?
scenes.visual: Predict card: donor labelled adrenomedullary trunk region; at home, sympathetic and adrenal cells (noradrenaline, adrenaline). Arrow to the vagal level of a chick.
scenes.narration: Predict. Take trunk crest from the adrenal level. At home it makes cells that release noradrenaline and adrenaline. Move it into the neck. Where will it go, and what transmitter will it use?

scenes.tts: They go where neck crest goes, into the gut wall. There they form enteric ganglia.
scenes.visual: Quail cells stream into the gut wall and gather into small ganglia.
scenes.narration: They go where neck crest goes, into the gut wall. There they form enteric ganglia.

scenes.tts: Some donor neurons are cholinergic: they use acetylcholine. The new site changed what the population made.
scenes.visual: Some donor-derived enteric neurons light up with the label acetylcholine. Note: population result.
scenes.narration: Some donor neurons are cholinergic: they use acetylcholine. The new site changed what the population made.

scenes.tts: Swap the other way, and neck crest placed at the adrenal level makes adrenal medulla and sympathetic derivatives.
scenes.visual: Reverse graft: vagal crest at the adrenomedullary trunk level; cells fill the adrenal medulla and a sympathetic ganglion.
scenes.narration: Swap the other way, and neck crest placed at the adrenal level makes adrenal medulla and sympathetic derivatives.

scenes.tts: The skeleton behaves differently. In most early grafts, trunk crest in the head made little or no cartilage.
scenes.visual: Two panels. Left: an early trunk-to-head graft; donor cells join the arches, cartilage mostly unlabelled. Right: trunk crest placed directly in developing head tissue, some labelled cartilage. Note: results depend on stage and graft context.
scenes.narration: The skeleton behaves differently. In most early grafts, trunk crest in the head made little or no cartilage.

scenes.tts: Under some conditions, trunk crest can make cartilage. So the start biases the options, and the surroundings help choose.
scenes.visual: Card: the start biases the options; the surroundings help choose.
scenes.narration: Under some conditions, trunk crest can make cartilage. So the start biases the options, and the surroundings help choose.

scenes.tts: Now predict. One cell in a dish makes neurons and pigment cells. Would it make both in the embryo?
scenes.visual: One cell in a well grows into a colony of neurons and pigment cells; beside it, an embryo with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Now predict. One cell in a dish makes neurons and pigment cells. Would it make both in the embryo?

scenes.tts: Not necessarily. A dish shows what a cell can make. Tracing in the embryo shows what it did make.
scenes.visual: Two labels: dish, can make; embryo, did make.
scenes.narration: Not necessarily. A dish shows what a cell can make. Tracing in the embryo shows what it did make.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty eight, both methods found some single cells that made several types. Whether the typical cell does is still debated.
scenes.caption: In 1988, both methods found some single cells that made several types. Whether the typical cell does is still debated.
scenes.visual: Two panels dated 1988: mixed and single-type clones in culture; a dye-filled clone spread over several derivatives in a chick.
scenes.narration: In 1988, both methods found some single cells that made several types. Whether the typical cell does is still debated.

scenes.tts: The takeaway. Move the cells, and the pattern appears. The start biases the options, and the journey helps choose.
scenes.visual: Closing card: move the cells; the start biases, the journey helps choose.
scenes.narration: The takeaway. Move the cells, and the pattern appears. The start biases the options, and the journey helps choose.
